question: What Is Negative Pressure in Pipelines?
body_html:
Negative pressure in pipelines means the pressure inside the pipe drops below atmospheric pressure, also called vacuum pressure. Outside pressure then pushes inward, which can buckle thin wall, plastic or ageing pipes and draw air or contaminants in through joints.

CauseExample
Pump suctionClogged filter while the pump keeps pulling
TransientsValve closure or pump trip causing column separation
DrainingClogged or missing air valve at high points
Thermal contractionHot liquid cooling in an isolated system
Fan suctionBlocked louvers or filters at duct inlets
